Paw & Whisker keeps the pricing model simple: there is a free browser-local profile for casual use, and an optional Plus plan for people who want more room to ask questions. There is also a separate Puppy Kit product with its own one-time checkout. The key difference is not just the price tag, but how each option fits a different kind of pet parent and a different style of use.

The free tier is designed for light, practical checking. It includes one browser-local profile, two AI questions per UTC day, all guides, a symptom-check tool, and a 48-food reference. No card is required. The limit is enforced on the server per signed browser session, and the profile is not synced to an account. Starting a conversation does not reset the allowance. Clearing cookies or using a different browser is not a reliable way to treat the system as a different identity, and that should not be presented as a bypass.

The Plus plan is advertised at $4.99 per month and includes unlimited questions plus photo questions through the existing Stripe link. The current purchase handling is existing and not newly audited. The site does not claim secure payment verification beyond that. The Puppy Kit is separate from Plus and is a one-time $12 purchase with its own checkout. It is positioned as a distinct product, not as part of the monthly plan.

This page is most useful when you think about what problem you are trying to solve. Some people only need occasional checks on a single ingredient, a symptom wording issue, or a quick read-through of a guide. Others want to send multiple follow-up questions in the same day, compare a few foods, or ask about a photo. Those are different use cases, so the best plan depends on your habits rather than a generic “best value” label.

Plan comparison

PlusUnlimited questions and photo questions via the existing Stripe linkSomeone who expects frequent use, longer back-and-forth, or image-based questionsCurrent purchase handling is existing, not newly audited; no diagnosis or care guarantees
Puppy KitSeparate one-time product at its own checkoutSomeone specifically looking for the puppy productNot part of the monthly Plus plan

If you are deciding between free and Plus, a practical question is how often you expect to come back to the site in a single day or over several days. If your main need is to verify one food, one label, or one symptom phrase, the free option may be enough. If you regularly want follow-up questions, the monthly plan is built for that style of use.

Another useful distinction is whether you want text-only checking or photo questions. The free tier covers guides, symptom-check and the 48-food reference, but photo questions are part of Plus. That matters if you prefer to show the product, ingredient list, or item directly rather than describe it in words. For food checks, the site also points people to the relevant toxic-food checker routes, such as /tools/toxic-food-checker/chocolate, /tools/toxic-food-checker/grapes, and /tools/toxic-food-checker/xylitol. These internal pages are better than guessing from memory when a package or ingredient list is in front of you.

How the free limit works

The free allowance is per signed browser session and is enforced on the server. That means the limit is not tied to an account that follows you everywhere, and it is not meant to be reset by simply starting a new conversation. It is also not reliable to assume that clearing cookies or changing browsers creates a fresh identity for the purpose of the allowance. The page should be clear about that rather than hinting at a workaround.

Because the profile is browser-local and not account-synced, the free tier is best thought of as a light-use starter mode. If you use one device for casual checking, that can feel straightforward. If you move between devices or browse in different browsers, the experience may feel less consistent because the profile does not travel with a central account.

How to choose the right option

  • Choose Free if you mainly want to browse guides, use the symptom-check, and make a small number of AI questions.
  • Choose Plus if you expect a lot of back-and-forth or want to ask with photos.
  • Choose the Puppy Kit if you want that separate one-time product rather than the monthly plan.
  • Use the food checkers when you need a direct food-specific route instead of broad browsing.
  • Use the plan that matches your actual habits, not the one that sounds biggest on paper.

When comparing services, a helpful question is not just “what is cheaper?” but “what will I actually use?” A lightweight free tier can be the better fit for occasional checks, while a paid plan can make more sense if you know you will come back repeatedly. That tradeoff is especially relevant when you are checking multiple foods, multiple pets, or several follow-up questions in one session.

Billing and access details

The Plus plan uses the existing Stripe link, and the Puppy Kit has its own separate checkout link. The site says cancel anytime, and refund requests within 7 days should be emailed to paul@pawandwhisker.net. Statutory rights are unaffected. The site also says there is an immediate PDF download after capture, while automated delivery is not enabled. Those details matter because they explain what happens after payment without promising a separate fulfilment system that is not there.

Privacy is also part of the decision. The data mentioned in the seed includes submitted questions and photos sent to the AI provider, plus the local profile. For many pet parents, that is a practical consideration: if you prefer a browser-local starter and do not want to share more than necessary, the free tier may suit that mindset. If you want unlimited use and photo questions, Plus is the relevant option, but it still comes with the same caution that no diagnosis or care guarantee is being made.

FAQs

Do I need a card to try the free plan?

No. The free option does not require a card.

Is the free limit based on my account?

No. The seed says it is enforced per signed browser session and the profile is not account-synced.

Can I reset the free allowance by clearing cookies or using another browser?

That is not reliable, and it should not be presented as a bypass.

What does Plus add that Free does not?

Plus is advertised as unlimited questions and photo questions.

Is the $4.99 monthly price live and verified?

The seed says it is advertised at that amount, but this page should not claim a newly audited verification.

Is the Puppy Kit part of Plus?

No. It is a separate one-time product with its own checkout.

Can I get a refund if I change my mind?

The seed says refund requests within 7 days go by email to paul@pawandwhisker.net, and statutory rights are unaffected.

Where should I go for food-specific checks?

Use the relevant toxic-food-checker route, such as the internal pages for chocolate, grapes or xylitol, rather than a broad species page.
